comparison: Both strongly support the finding of variable bacterial burdens across wild-derived mouse strains (C33-C37, C110). OpenEval emphasizes CFU data and statistical significance in Figures 1B-D, while peer reviewers explicitly praise this as a major achievement, with all three reviewers acknowledging the successful identification of susceptible strains and increased phenotypic diversity.

Both support the correlation between T cells/B cells and infection control (C4, C44). OpenEval cites correlation analysis in Figures 2F-I with Spearman statistics. Peer reviewers (R1, R2) explicitly confirm these correlations were observed and note the data are convincing. Peer R2 also addresses C135 (B cell correlation) which OpenEval covers separately in R27.

Both support the lack of IFN-γ correlation with bacterial burden (C5, C48-C49, C131-C132). OpenEval cites Figures 2K-M showing this deviation from standard B6 mice. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly notes infection control correlated 'not necessarily with the percentage of interferon-gamma producing cells,' treating this as an important discovery that challenges conventional understanding.

Both strongly support the finding that MANB and MANC have similar neutrophil numbers but different outcomes (C6, C67-C69). OpenEval cites Figures 4A-C as key evidence. Peer Reviewer 1 highlights this as revealing 'very unique biology of neutrophils' and notes 'some mouse strains could be resistant to infection even with high numbers of neutrophils.' Peer R2 confirms 'comparable numbers of neutrophils but drastically different bacterial burdens.'

OpenEval strongly supports neutrophil depletion findings (C70-C72, C113-C114) based on Figures 4D-F showing dramatic MANC effects. Peer reviewers acknowledge the data but express UNCERTAIN evaluation due to concerns about descriptive nature and lack of functional/mechanistic validation. Reviewer 1 states 'functional and mechanistic investigations are lacking' regarding neutrophil subset functions. The depletion provides some functional evidence but reviewers want deeper mechanistic understanding.

OpenEval supports histological findings of neutrophil organization differences (C73-C75, C115) based on immunofluorescence in Figures 4G-J. This is part of the broader neutrophil characterization that peer reviewers find descriptive but lacking mechanistic depth (R5 UNCERTAIN evaluation covers C73-C75, C115 among other neutrophil claims).

OpenEval supports scRNAseq clustering showing distinct MANC neutrophils (C7, C76-C80) based on Figures 4K-L. Peer reviewers acknowledge the transcriptional characterization but express concerns about lack of functional validation (UNCERTAIN). The clustering data are accepted but reviewers want mechanistic investigation beyond transcriptional profiles.

OpenEval supports GO enrichment and gene expression findings (C81-C83, C116-C117) from Figure 4M and 5A. These are part of the transcriptional characterization that peer reviewers find descriptive (UNCERTAIN in R5). Peer R2 notes identification of 'potentially tissue-destructive mediators' but overall reviewers want functional validation.

OpenEval supports comparison with Sp140-/- showing unique MANC neutrophil phenotype (C84-C87, C118) based on Figures 5A and supplements. This comparison is part of the transcriptional analysis that peer reviewers acknowledge but find needs mechanistic follow-up (covered in R5 UNCERTAIN evaluation).

OpenEval supports distinct transcriptional signatures between MANC and Sp140-/- neutrophils (C91, C120) from Figure 5B. This genotype-specific characterization is part of the descriptive analysis that peer reviewers accept but want functionally validated (R5 UNCERTAIN includes C91, C120).

OpenEval supports neutrophil staging analysis showing immature neutrophils in MANC (C92-C93) from Figure 5C. This finding is part of the comprehensive neutrophil characterization that peer reviewers acknowledge but find needs deeper mechanistic investigation (R5 UNCERTAIN includes C92-C93).

Both support the in vitro macrophage findings (C51-C55, C60). OpenEval cites Figures 3A-C showing comparable/better bacterial control by Manaus macrophages. Peer Reviewer 2 notes the study was 'elegantly supplemented with in vitro macrophage infections' and no reviewer challenges the conclusion that macrophage defects don't explain MANC susceptibility.

OpenEval supports type I IFN findings (C56-C59) from Figure 3D showing lack of correlation with susceptibility. Peer reviewers accept the macrophage characterization (R6) which includes these type I IFN observations as part of ruling out macrophage-intrinsic defects.

Perfect claim overlap (C94-C99). Both support T cell characterization findings showing no major phenotypic differences. OpenEval cites Figure 4 supplement 2B. Peer reviewers accept these data as supporting the conclusion that neutrophils, not T cell intrinsic defects, drive MANC susceptibility.

Perfect claim overlap (C100-C105). Both support unusual S100a8/a9 expression in MANC macrophages. OpenEval cites Figure 6A and supplements. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of comprehensive single-cell analysis praised by Reviewer 2, supporting widespread neutrophil-associated gene expression in MANC.

Perfect claim overlap (C106-C109). Both support widespread neutrophil gene expression across cell types in MANC. OpenEval cites Figures 6B-C and ImmGen comparison. Peer reviewers accept this finding as part of comprehensive characterization, with R2 noting identification of tissue-destructive mediators.

Both support characterization of the wild-derived mouse resource (C25-C26, C28-C30). OpenEval emphasizes documentation through citations and Figure 1A. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly praises the 'innovative generation and use of mouse models' and notes deposition at Jackson Laboratory as making these 'valuable resources available to the scientific community.'

Both support lack of weight/sex effects at early timepoint (C39-C40). OpenEval cites correlation analysis in Figure 1 supplement 1E-F. Peer reviewers accept these as appropriate controls and characterization, with no challenges to the negative findings.

Partial overlap on C3 (immune cell variability). OpenEval groups C3 with C42-C43 focusing on flow cytometry showing variability with neutrophils most dramatic. Peer R1 acknowledges overall variability findings as part of the successful demonstration of increased phenotypic diversity.

Partial overlap on C64 (neutrophil-CFU correlation). OpenEval R8 focuses on strong positive correlation (C45-C46, C64) from Figure 2J. Peer R4 addresses broader neutrophil heterogeneity findings (C6, C63-C69) including that neutrophil number alone doesn't determine outcome.

Partial overlap on Manaus neutrophil heterogeneity (C63, C65-C66). OpenEval emphasizes high neutrophils with variable CFU and decreased correlation. Peer R4 broadly supports neutrophil heterogeneity findings, with R1 highlighting 'diverse functions of neutrophils' as important information.

Partial overlap on C135 (B cell correlation). OpenEval notes B cell correlation as observation requiring future investigation. Peer R2 includes C135 in broader discussion of correlations with infection control, accepting the finding without challenge.

OpenEval supports background/rationale claims (C1-C2, C8-C11) about TB heterogeneity and mouse model limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are background claims establishing study rationale rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval supports gene expression patterns including high Il1rn in MANB (C88-C90) from Figure 5A. No specific peer review evaluation found for these particular gene expression claims, though they are part of the broader transcriptional analysis.

OpenEval rates C119, C133 as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly stated hypotheses requiring additional experiments (spatial analysis, mechanistic studies). No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative claims about mechanisms.

OpenEval supports S100a8/a9 literature context claims (C121-C124) through citations. No specific peer review evaluation found, though peer R9 acknowledges identification of tissue-destructive mediators including S100 proteins.

OpenEval supports IFN-γ complexity literature claims (C125-C130) through multiple citations providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these are literature context claims rather than novel findings.

OpenEval supports extensive background literature claims (C12-C24, C47, C56, C61-C62, C111-C112) as established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these provide necessary background but are not novel findings requiring peer assessment.
